title: Meadowbrook Retail Infosec Readiness Notebook
content:
Executive summary:

This is the working notebook for the Meadowbrook Retail POC (security readiness stream). Purpose: capture infosec questionnaire answers, evidence pointers, workshop outputs, and an action plan for an internal audit / customer review. Document is intentionally informal — collates raw notes from the 2025-10-08 technical workshop and the follow-up security Q&A.

High-level status (snapshot):
- Scope: Dedicated + Private (VPC) deployment with HSM-backed keys for payment data tokenization, network egress controls to Meadowbrook IP ranges, and audit log export to customer SIEM.
- Current readiness: partial. Major items remaining: HSM integration proof, long-term retention proof for audit logs, and SOC2 artifact linking for dedicated controller processes.
- Next major milestone: deliver evidence bundle for Meadowbrook internal audit (target 2025-12-05).

Workshop recap (2025-10-08):
- Attendees: Priya (SE lead), Ethan (security SWE), Maya (SRE), Samuel (customer security lead, Meadowbrook), Jordan (solution architect).
- Format: 2-hour remote workshop, breakout on KMS/HSM, network architecture, and logging/retention.
- Key decisions: use customer-managed AWS KMS CMK in Dedicated; schedule HSM validation for 2025-11-03; use TLS mutual auth for service-to-service traffic.
- Open questions raised by Meadowbrook: data residency proofs, key custody flow during failover, retention proof for 90-day logs, and process for emergency key rotation.

Questionnaire (selected Qs + draft responses):
Q: Where are customer tokens and PII stored?
A: Application-level tokens (short-lived) are stored only in encrypted Redis KV inside the Dedicated cluster; persistent artifacts (charged metadata) are stored in encrypted S3 buckets within the customer VPC when on Private. We never persist raw PAN; tokenization handled by customer-approved HSM/KMS in their account. (See evidence id E-03, E-07)

Q: Who has access to KMS keys?
A: Customer is configured as the owner of the KMS CMK; Redwood holds no administrative access in Private deployment. For Dedicated with Redwood-managed KMS, access is restricted to a dedicated control-plane role with MFA and just-in-time approval; admin actions logged to immutable CloudTrail forwarded to customer SIEM. (See E-05, E-09)

Q: How do you prove logs are immutable and retained?
A: We forward audit logs to a write-once S3 prefix with bucket lock enabled and replication to customer-controlled archival account. Retention is configured per contract (default 90 days); snapshots exported as signed manifests. (See E-11, E-12)

Evidence index (working) — short ids point to artifacts we'll attach to the bundle:
- E-01: Network diagram (annotated) — private-dedicated-meadowbrook-network-2025-10.png (diagram includes CIDR, peering, Transit GW notes)
- E-02: VPC peering justification & peering config snippets (terraform plan excerpt)
- E-03: Tokenization flow doc — pseudocode and sequence diagram (token-flow.md)
- E-04: KMS policy sample (customer-owned CMK) — kms-policy-meadowbrook.json
- E-05: Control plane admin role audit trail snippet (CloudTrail events) — cloudtrail-admin-2025-10.log
- E-06: Mutual TLS cert exchange step-by-step (Workshop notes) — mTLS-handshake-notes.txt
- E-07: HSM integration test report (planned 2025-11-03) — hsm-validation-plan.md
- E-08: SIEM ingestion config (customer side) — siem-ingest-elk.json
- E-09: RBAC matrix for Dedicated nodes (who can deploy, escalate) — rbac-dedicated-matrix.csv
- E-10: Incident response runbook extract (redwood-incident-runbook.pdf)
- E-11: S3 bucket-lock proof + replication manifest (s3-lock-manifest-2025-10.json)
- E-12: Signed log snapshots (sha256 sums) — logs-snapshot-2025-10.sig

Notes on evidence collection: some artifacts are generated by infra (CloudTrail, bucket manifests). Others are authored (diagrams, runbooks). Need to avoid sending production credentials; provide redacted snippets and access-controlled signed manifests.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ethan Brooks — complete KMS policy redaction and E-04 finalization — due 2025-10-24
- Maya Lin — schedule HSM validation window & produce E-07 test report — due 2025-11-05
- Priya Nair — assemble zip bundle, sign manifest, and upload to customer secure share — due 2025-11-22
- Jordan Ruiz — confirm network egress IPs and create final annotated diagram (E-01) — due 2025-10-20
- Samuel Park (customer) — confirm acceptance criteria for log retention and sign off on manifest delivery method — due 2025-11-10

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Meadowbrook requires evidence of HSM key ceremony in their AWS account. Mitigation: run a supervised validation session (E-07) and capture screen-recorded proof and signed witnesses.
- Risk: Customer legal wants vendor to attest no access to PII. Mitigation: provide architecture screenshots showing customer-owned KMS and an excerpt of the RBAC matrix (E-04, E-09), and add a signed attestation template.
- Risk: Timebox pressure — audit date requested earlier than readiness. Mitigation: prioritize E-11 (log immutability manifest) and E-05 (control plane audit snippet) for immediate delivery.

Technical appendix (raw notes, commands):
- Terraform snippet (redacted):
  resource "aws_kms_key" "meadowbrook_cmk" {
    description = "Customer-owned CMK for Meadowbrook POC — key policy shows only customer principals"
    deletion_window_in_days = 7
  }

- Example CloudTrail query (saved):
  SELECT eventTime, eventName, userIdentity.arn FROM $CT WHERE eventName = 'DisableKey' LIMIT 50

- Curl sample to fetch signed manifest (internal test only):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \n    -o s3-lock-manifest-2025-10.json \n    https://internal.artifacts.redwood/test-bundles/meadowbrook/s3-lock-manifest

Workshop follow-ups (notes to self):
- Prepare an incident timeline template with redaction guidance — customers ask often how to map Redwood ID -> customer ticketing.
- Confirm whether Dedicated backup snapshots are controllable by mailbox retention policies (Maya to check with infra ops).
- Draft a short attestation letter for customers asserting no Redwood admin key access in Private deployments (legal to review).

Customer communication draft (for review):
Subject: Meadowbrook — Infosec evidence bundle and next steps\n
Hi Samuel / Meadowbrook security team,\n
Thanks again for the workshop. Attached is a preliminary evidence bundle and a short checklist of outstanding items we will complete before the audit. We plan to run the HSM validation on 2025-11-03 (please confirm delegate).\n
Action items required from Meadowbrook: confirmation of SIEM ingest endpoint, and acceptance of signed log manifest transfer method.\n
Best,\nPriya (on behalf of Redwood Solutions Engineering)

References & cross-links:
- Confluence POC master page (link in linked_artifacts)
- Jira ticket JIRA-SEC-4127 (access request & documentation)
- Internal PR for redaction tooling (linked_artifacts)

Version history (work-in-progress):
- 2025-10-08: initial workshop notes captured
- 2025-10-15: assembled draft evidence index and initial Q&A answers
- 2025-10-24: KMS policy redaction (E-04) expected
- 2025-11-03: HSM validation scheduled
- 2025-11-20: current doc — preparing final bundle

----
Metadata checklist (for audit pack):
- all items listed E-01..E-12 present? (partial)
- each evidence item has a redaction flag + signer (TBD)
- manifest signed with Redwood bundle key and timestamped

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally conversational. Add missing artifacts directly into the shared folder and ping me in #p-se-meadowbrook. If you are adding logs, include a sha256 signature and an access manifest.

(END)
